mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a single month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the tightening signal, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% in a single month signals a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors react to the potential economic slowdown.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 70% of triggered instances despite the labor market weakening signal, or if the correlation between UNRATE increases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP growth over two consecutive quarters signals a weakening demand environment, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings expectations adjust downwards.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of periods following two consecutive quarters of GDP decline, or if the correlation between GDP decline and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production by more than 2% in a single month signals a strong supply-side response, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as increased production capacity supports economic growth and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the strong supply-side signal, or if the correlation between INDPRO increases and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in retail and food services sales by more than 1% in a single month signals a weakening consumer demand, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer-driven sectors represent a significant portion of the index.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the consumer demand weakening signal, or if the correlation between RSAFS decreases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls by more than 300,000 in a single month signals a strengthening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors interpret this as a sign of robust economic growth.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 70% of triggered instances despite the strong labor market signal, or if the correlation between PAYEMS increases and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts and a decrease in unemployment rate signals a strengthening demand environment, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as both indicators suggest robust economic activity.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases > 5% in 1 month and UNRATE decreases > 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the strong demand signal, or if the joint effect of HOUST increase and UNRATE decrease on positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained low inflation environment, indicated by CPIAUCSL remaining below 2% for three consecutive months, signals a stable monetary policy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as stable prices support consumer spending and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the stable inflation signal, or if the correlation between low CPIAUCSL and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
